initial_prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: ONE three-panel visual-style comparison board for a Korean fictional horror channel, a preview experiment only. Input image 1 is a SCENE GEOMETRY reference, NOT a target to overwrite and NOT a photographic style reference. Show the SAME closed Korean kids cafe from the SAME doorway viewpoint in three clearly separated horizontal 16:9 panels stacked vertically, with small charcoal gutters and a small clean left-aligned letter A, B, C on each gutter. Preserve blue enclosed ball pit at back LEFT, yellow slide at back RIGHT, two plain rectangular tables in middle, open brown staff-room door front RIGHT, tiled floor. Place the SAME single muted red ball with one black dash on the foreground floor in all three panels; no people, children, faces, entity, gore, logos, captions or additional text. Each panel must be UNMISTAKABLY NONPHOTOGRAPHIC hand-drawn illustration: never a photo with a filter. All panels ominous, oppressive, quiet, adult horror, most surfaces in a deep desaturated shadow; faint cyan side light from one weak ceiling lamp and tiny dirty amber door spill, not bright uniform lighting. Red ball silhouette and doorway silhouette must still read on a phone. Panel A: dark painterly gouache/oil illustration, broad uneven impasto brush marks, broken softened edges, tactile coarse matte canvas, simplified material details and lost edges in shadows, restrained moss teal, charcoal navy, dirty ivory and muted red. No meticulous photoreal texture. This is the recommended balance of disturbing atmosphere and clear physical clues. Panel B: charcoal and dry ink horror drawing on dark stained paper, expressive dense black strokes and rough rubbed graphite edges, almost monochrome with only the small muted red ball, warped shadows but keep furniture physically coherent. Panel C: gritty mature 2D hand-painted animation background, irregular drawn contours, simplified shadow blocks, cel-like forms and painted grain, restrained low saturation teal-gray with yellow slide almost ochre, not cute, not polished vector, not glossy CGI. Keep panels distinctly different in medium. No generic fog blanket or heavy blur hiding the clue; uncertainty should come from darkness, selective edges, and unsettling empty space. Do not copy a known artist or movie frame. Overall portrait comparison board, all three landscape panels large and legible, equal sizes.
revision_prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: the supplied three-panel horror illustration comparison board. Preserve exactly the three equal stacked landscape panels, small A/B/C labels, room composition, back-left blue ball pit/back-right yellow slide/two rectangular tables/open front-right brown door, single muted red foreground ball with one black dash, no human/creature. Make ALL panels meaningfully LESS SHARP and MORE OMINOUS. They must clearly be drawings, not heavily textured photographs. Most importantly REMOVE fine tile detail, shiny floor reflection, scratch/peeling/decay detail: the cafe is an intact ordinary functioning room at closing, NOT an abandoned ruined building. Medium texture is pigment and marks on the illustration surface, NOT actual mold/damage in the depicted room. A: drastically simplify into broad matte gouache brush masses on coarse paper, little material rendering, irregular soft/lost edges, grouped shadows obscure portions of table legs/walls/far ceiling, limited charcoal navy/dirty teal/gray umber colors, local ivory lamp glint and red ball remain readable. This top panel must look like an eerie hand-painted horror storybook background, with painterly mass shapes rather than photo-perfect microtexture. B: dense black charcoal/ink expressionist drawing with spare rubbed highlights, less line detail, unsettling expansive black shadows, coarse dry graphite pigment on dark paper, retain the muted red clue, intact architectural geometry no physical cracks. C: mature hand-drawn 2D animation background with simplified painted contours/flat shadow shapes and softer background, deep low-saturation colors and heavier shadow than before, not photorealistic, not glossy videogame/CGI/cute. Turn off the right ceiling light in all panels; retain one faint narrow left/back light and a weak dirty amber rim from the doorway. The foreground ball remains readable by silhouette and muted red contrast, not a spotlight or shiny highlight. No heavy Gaussian blur, no whole-frame black, no uniform gray veil, no new objects/text/characters. Preserve the viewpoint and continuity while allowing negative-space shadows and clearly nonphotographic forms.
